6807               cv256
6808               	; 		' HE IS STANDING ON A STEP, so he moves at the STEP's rate: 2 px
6809               	; 		' across and 1 up PER PASS -- the staircase's own slope, and exactly
6810               	; 		' what one phase of esc_tick moves the pattern by.
6811               	; 		'
6812               	; 		' NOT `fdv`, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT. Everything else in this loop
6813               	; 		' is paced by the frame delta, and pacing him that way too made him
6814               	; 		' outrun the steps the moment a pass cost more than one frame: his
6815               	; 		' feet started planted on a tread and ended floating above it.
6816               	; 		' Pacing the ANIMATION by fdv instead is worse -- four phases cannot
6817               	; 		' be stepped by 2 or 3 without aliasing, and the staircase runs
6818               	; 		' backwards (see esc_tick). The only arrangement that cannot drift
6819               	; 		' is the one where both are driven by the same fixed step, so the
6820               	; 		' rider is clocked by the pass, like the steps he is standing on.
6821               	; 		'
6822               	; 		' THE FIRST FEW PASSES ARE THE STEP ON. Walking on, his feet are on
6823               	; 		' the floor and the bottom tread is 4 to 7 px above them, so he
6824               	; 		' climbs at 2 px a pass until he catches it (the tread is rising at

7363               	; 		' him a few pixels and made NO sound at all. That does not read as
7364               	; 		' a short step, it reads as the controls being ignored, and it is

7366               	; 		' jump, or edging around a hazard.

8287               	;
8288               	; 	' THE VICTROLA, AS CHARACTERS. It never moves, so a sprite spent a
8289               	; 	' scan-line slot on something that can be painted once when the screen is
8290               	; 	' drawn -- and at one 16x16 sprite it could only ever be one colour and
8291               	; 	' one size. Four cells is twice the area for no sprite at all.
8292               	; 	'
8293               	; 	' It stands ON the slab, so it fills the band's rows 2 and 3; row 4 is
8294               	; 	' the floor bar itself -- and a PRIZE uses those same two rows.
8295               	; 	'
8296               	; 	' THEY CAN SHARE A BAND, AND THE CLAIM THAT USED TO BE HERE WAS WRONG.
8297               	; 	' It said the two never share a screen because "genstore keeps prizes off
8298               	; 	' the screens that carry hazards". That stopped being true the moment
8299               	; 	' hazard placement moved into the per-Krook stor_lvl table, and nothing
8300               	; 	' noticed, because the prize table is not part of the level table and
8301               	; 	' every check was written about one object at a time. Two money bags ended
8302               	; 	' up standing on a radio -- not fighting it, since the two routines poke
8303               	; 	' different cells and the later writer simply wins, so they read as one
8304               	; 	' merged object.
8305               	; 	'
8306               	; 	' WHAT KEEPS THEM APART IS COLUMNS. A radio stands at column 7, 15 or 23
8307               	; 	' (see lrc below); genstore's _off_the_rack nudges a prize clear of all
8308               	; 	' three, and checklevels.py reads that arithmetic back out of THIS file
8309               	; 	' and fails the build on any overlap.
8310               	; 	'
8311               	; 	' rdall = 1 paints all four cells, 0 repaints only the top-right one --
8312               	; 	' the pulse. Same address arithmetic either way, so the two cannot drift.
8313               	; 	' A BEAM TOP HANGS OUT OF THE FLOOR ABOVE, and the beam it belongs to has
8314               	; 	' just been taken away. `beam_tops` stamps SLABP -- the floor bar with the
8315               	; 	' support carried up through its lower three pixel rows -- into the slab
8316               	; 	' row above every pillar, and it runs BEFORE the radios and prizes are
8317               	; 	' placed. Clearing a pillar's own cells therefore left three grey pixels
8318               	; 	' dangling from the ceiling with nothing under them.
8319               	; 	'
8320               	; 	' TESTED, NOT ASSUMED: only SLABP is put back to SLAB. The row above the
8321               	; 	' top shopping floor is the ROOF DECK, a different character altogether,
8322               	; 	' and writing a floor bar over it would punch a hole in the roof.
8323               	; 	' A SHELF RUN IS FIVE CELLS WIDE and a radio covers two, so one standing
8324               	; 	' on a counter punched a hole through its middle and left the ends either
8325               	; 	' side -- the same incoherence the dangling pillar had, and worse, because
8326               	; 	' a counter reads as one object. The whole unit goes: walk outward along
8327               	; 	' the band's row 2 while the cell is still a shelf top, clearing it and
8328               	; 	' its bottom half together.
8329               	; 	'
8330               	; 	' Bounded at eight steps. The runs are five, so eight is slack rather
8331               	; 	' than a guess -- and an unbounded walk would run off the end of the row
8332               	; 	' if the name table ever held something unexpected.
8333               	; 	#if NES
8334               	; 	' WHAT THE TEMPLATE PUT IN THIS CELL, for a target that cannot read its
8335               	; 	' own video memory back. #nta is the offset INSIDE the band (0-159) and
8336               	; 	' nbl is the band; the answer is the byte SCREEN blitted there.
8337               	; 	'
8338               	; 	' This is the same arithmetic the blit itself does in draw_band --
8339               	; 	' template id out of stor_ix for (band, screen), times 160, plus the
8340               	; 	' offset -- so the two cannot disagree about what is on screen. It is
8341               	; 	' reading what the cell MEANS, not guessing from where the cell is: a
8342               	; 	' coordinate is a fact about this layout, the character is a fact about
8343               	; 	' the world, and only the second is safe to erase on.
8344               	; nes_tpl:
8345               	; 	nti = lv8(nbl)
8346               	; 	nti = nti + klsc
8347               	; 	#ntb = #stix + nti
8348               	; 	ntd = PEEK(#ntb)
8349               	; 	#ntc = #tsrc(ntd)
8350               	; 	#ntc = #ntc + #nta
8351               	; 	#ntc = #ntc + #sttp
8352               	; 	ntv = PEEK(#ntc)
8353               	; 	RETURN
8354               	; 	#endif
8355               	;
8356               	; wipe_shelf:
8357               cvb_WIPE_SHELF

8437               	; 	' A PILLAR'S CAP MAY BE CLEARED; AN END WALL'S MAY NOT. beam_one stamps
8438               	; 	' both into the slab row of the band above, but they mean different
8439               	; 	' things. SLABP is the top of a free-standing pillar: a radio or a prize
8440               	; 	' stands in front of the pillar, so leaving its cap up there hangs a grey
8441               	; 	' stub over the fixture and that is what this routine exists to remove.

8443               	; 	' beam_one, they are the two edge cases -- and there they are the

8445               	; 	' above. Clearing those took the support out from under the storey above
8446               	; 	' at the very edge of the screen, so the second floor visibly rested on
8447               	; 	' nothing.
8448               	; 	'
8449               	; 	' It could only ever show on the ESCALATOR screens, which is exactly how
8450               	; 	' it was reported -- one side, then mirrored on the other. The flight
8451               	; 	' fills the middle of an escalator band, so that screen's radio or prize
8452               	; 	' is pushed right out against the end wall; on every other screen no
8453               	; 	' fixture sits close enough for the two-cell clear at #bca and #bca+1 to

8458               	; 	' ABOVE each band, out of the pillar-column table -- so on the NES this
8459               	; 	' asks that same table rather than the PPU, and #bca sits one row above
8460               	; 	' the band, which is why it cannot go through nes_tpl.
8461               	; 	'

8463               	; 	' carry SLABE/ROOFSE, the building's OUTSIDE WALL, not a pillar cap --

9079               	; upd_obst:

9081               	; 	' ONE ACCUMULATOR PER KIND, NOT PER SLOT. Every hazard of a kind moves at
9082               	; 	' that kind's speed, so three calls a pass serve all eight slots.
9083               	; 	'
9084               	; 	' Per-slot would have meant up to eight calls of O(fdv) work every pass --
9085               	; 	' the positive feedback loop CLAUDE.md 3A warns about, where a slow pass is
9086               	; 	' made slower by the very code meant to take the loop rate out of the
9087               	; 	' game's behaviour. It also saves the eight bytes an obacc() would cost,
9088               	; 	' and ColecoVision RAM is the tighter budget.
9089               	; 	pacc = oacb
9090 D532 D820  54 	movb @cvb_OACB,@cvb_PACC
     D534 20D1     
     D536 2130

9379               	;
9380               	; 	' ONE STEP OF A FRACTIONAL SPEED, FOR WHOEVER IS MOVING.
9381               	; 	'
9382               	; 	' `pacc` in and out, `psp64` in (sixty-fourths of a pixel per FRAME),
9383               	; 	' `pspd` out (whole pixels this pass). CVBasic has no locals, so the caller
9384               	; 	' stages its own accumulator in and takes it back out; that costs four
9385               	; 	' statements against the fourteen this used to be, written out per actor.
9386               	; 	'
9387               	; 	' Harry had the only copy. Kelly, the hazards and the bounce phase all need
9388               	; 	' the same thing -- everything the round clock judges has to advance by
9389               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAMES, or the loop rate becomes a difficulty dial and where the
9390               	; 	' player stands decides the outcome (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
9391               	; 	'
9392               	; 	' TWO DRAINS CAP THE STEP AT 2 PER FRAME whatever psp64 says (CLAUDE.md
9393               	; 	' 3A: N drains cap the speed at N, and the surplus leaks into a byte that
9394               	; 	' wraps). Every caller is under that: Kelly 102/64 = 1.6, the fastest
9395               	; 	' hazard 76/64 = 1.2, Harry 57/64 = 0.9, the bounce phase 25/64 = 0.4.
9396               	; 	'
9397               	; 	' FIVE FRAMES, AND THREE WAS TOO FEW. At 2 px a frame five frames is 10 px,
9398               	; 	' and to skip a position window an actor must start outside it on one side
9399               	; 	' and land outside on the other, which needs 12. Three was the original bug
9400               	; 	' in miniature: the lift screen runs at almost exactly 20 passes a second,
9401               	; 	' which IS fdv = 3, so every hitch there lost a frame. The clamp exists for
9402               	; 	' a genuine stall and at five it only fires for one.

9891               	; 	' THE SIXTEENTH-PIXEL ACCUMULATOR. hx is one unsigned byte per screen
9892               	; 	' (2), so there is nowhere to keep a fraction -- the fraction lives here
9893               	; 	' and is spent as whole pixels. THREE IFs, not a loop and not a divide:
9894               	; 	' `%` and `/` both compile to a real TMS9900 DIV (CLAUDE.md 3A) and this
9895               	; 	' runs every pass.
9896               	; 	'
9897               	; 	' THE NUMBER OF DRAINS IS A CEILING ON THE SPEED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE
9898               	; 	' POINT OF THIS COMMENT. Each IF can spend one whole pixel, so N drains
9899               	; 	' cap hspd at N px per pass NO MATTER WHAT hsp64 SAYS. The invariant is:
9900               	; 	'
9901               	; 	'     hacc is under 16 on entry, and hsp64 is at most 48,
9902               	; 	'     so hacc is under 64 here and three drains always suffice.
9903               	; 	'
9904               	; 	' KEEP hsp64 <= 48. This was quarter-pixels with TWO drains and the same
9905               	; 	' invariant written the same way -- "hsp4 is at most 8, so it can never
9906               	; 	' need a third" -- and it was correct until somebody set hsp4 = 9 without
9907               	; 	' re-reading it. The crook then ran at a flat 2.0 px/pass while every
9908               	; 	' comment, the design table and assets/checkchase.py all said 2.25, and
9909               	; 	' the surplus quarter leaked into hacc and wrapped the byte every 256
9910               	; 	' passes. Nothing failed; he simply arrived two thirds of a screen short
9911               	; 	' of his own escape. checkchase.py now counts these IFs and refuses a
9912               	; 	' speed the drains cannot deliver.
9913               	; 	'
9914               	; 	' 7, NOT 6, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED. Tracked off the reference video
9915               	; 	' (DESIGN.md 4a), the 2600's Kelly covers 0.40 screen widths a second and
9916               	; 	' its Harry 0.193 -- a ratio of 2.07. At hsp4 = 6 ours was 2.67, and the
9917               	; 	' crook visibly strolled. 7 brings it to 2.29. 8 would match the original
9918               	; 	' exactly and cannot be used: Kelly's route here is 1.95x Harry's, so a
9919               	; 	' speed ratio of 2.0 leaves the on-foot chase 0.2 s of slack, which is no
9920               	; 	' chase at all. checkchase.py holds the line.
9921               	; 	' STILL RUNNING FROM THE STAIRS -- and this has to come BEFORE the move,

9924               	; 	' the run cycle and did not travel a pixel. He stood at the foot of the

10022               	; 	' HE WALKS BY REAL TIME, NOT BY LOOP PASS -- one accumulate-and-drain per
10023               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAME rather than per pass. Everything that moves here used to be
10024               	; 	' per pass while the CLOCK is paced by the frame delta, so a busy screen
10025               	; 	' slowed Harry in real seconds and the clock did not slow with him: the
10026               	; 	' same uninterrupted escape finished with nine timer units in hand from a
10027               	; 	' light screen and none at all from the lift screen, decided by where the
10028               	; 	' player happened to be standing. Now he covers the same ground per second
10029               	; 	' wherever anybody is (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
10030               	; 	'
10031               	; 	' A LOOP, NOT A MULTIPLY. `*` compiles to a real TMS9900 MPY, and reading a
10032               	; 	' 16-bit variable straight after one returns the product's HIGH word
10033               	; 	' (CLAUDE.md 3A). fdv is 1..3 here, so this is at most three adds.
10034               	; 	'
10035               	; 	' SIXTY-FOURTHS, AND ONLY TWO DRAINS -- both fall out of accumulating per
10036               	; 	' FRAME instead of per pass. He covers under a pixel a frame, so two drains
10037               	; 	' are ample where the per-pass version needed three; and the finer unit is
10038               	; 	' what makes the speed tunable at all. In sixteenths one step was about six
10039               	; 	' SECONDS of his route, so nothing landed near the buzzer; in sixty-fourths
10040               	; 	' it is about one and a half. Keep hsp64 <= 128: hacc is under 64 on entry,
10041               	; 	' so 64 + 128 stays inside a byte and two drains always suffice.
10042               	; 	'
10043               	; 	' AND THE STEP IS CLAMPED TO THREE FRAMES' WORTH, WHICH IS NOT A DETAIL.
10044               	; 	' Two tests sample his position once a pass and neither interpolates:
10045               	; 	'
10046               	; 	'   ARRIVAL   `hdx < 6` around the escalator or the roof door -- an ELEVEN
10047               	; 	'             pixel window. A step over 10 px can jump clean across it and
10048               	; 	'             he never arrives at all.
10049               	; 	'   THE CATCH `hdd < CATCHR` is 12, a 23-wide band, and Kelly closes 4 of
10050               	; 	'             it himself -- so Harry over ~18 px could pass through the Kop
10051               	; 	'             between two passes without either sample being inside it.
10052               	; 	'
10053               	; 	' The clamp and the drains live in pace_step now, with the reasoning; the
10054               	; 	' numbers above are what sized them. Measured: TIME 02 on the lift screen
10055               	; 	' against TIME 04 on a light one when the clamp was 3, and 00 against 09
10056               	; 	' before any of this.

10058               	; 	' The ESCALATOR RIDE is deliberately untouched: it returns above this,
10059               	; 	' clocked one step per pass to stay locked to the moving staircase. A rider

10061               	; 	' steps run backwards (CLAUDE.md 3A, DESIGN.md 0f). It is about 3% of his
10062               	; 	' journey.

10527               	;
10528               	; 	' ======================================================================
10529               	; 	' COLLISIONS -- pure arithmetic against RAM, no VDP reads
10530               	; 	' ======================================================================
10531               	; 	' Kelly's box is [kfh, kfh + kh) above the slab; an obstacle's is
10532               	; 	' [ohb, oht). The ball's inset hitbox is what makes 8..10 avoidable both
10533               	; 	' ways -- without it there is a height at which the ball can be neither
10534               	; 	' jumped nor ducked, and an unavoidable hazard is not difficulty.
10535               	; 	' ONE HIT PER CONTACT, WITH A REFRACTORY PERIOD.
10536               	; 	'
10537               	; 	' The overlap test is true on every frame the player is touching
10538               	; 	' something, so with no latch at all one clumsy cart charges nine seconds
10539               	; 	' several times over -- and what the player sees is the clock jumping by
10540               	; 	' 27, from which the only available conclusion is that the penalty is
10541               	; 	' broken.
10542               	; 	'
10543               	; 	' A latch that clears on the first non-overlapping frame is still not
10544               	; 	' enough, and the case that breaks it is the BOUNCING BALL: it rises off
10545               	; 	' the player between bounces, which is a genuine loss of contact, so a
10546               	; 	' player standing still under one is taxed on every single bounce while
10547               	; 	' being given no opportunity to do anything about it. Technically two
10548               	; 	' collisions; in play, one situation.
10549               	; 	'
10550               	; 	' So obht() is a countdown, not a flag. A hit sets it to HITREF; it ticks
10551               	; 	' down only while the player is CLEAR, and the same obstacle cannot charge

10921               	; 	' THE FLOOR CLEARS WHEN YOU ARE HIT, and stays clear until you re-enter
10922               	; 	' the screen. Nine seconds is a heavy penalty on a fifty-unit clock, and
10923               	; 	' taking it while still standing among the things that charged it -- with
10924               	; 	' a second hazard 48 px behind the first -- is how one mistake becomes
10925               	; 	' three. Clearing the row makes the penalty a single event you can walk
10926               	; 	' away from.
10927               	; 	'
10928               	; 	' BOTH SLOTS, WHATEVER IS IN THEM. Radios used to be exempt: they are
10929               	; 	' CHARACTERS stamped into the name table rather than sprites, so zeroing
10930               	; 	' the kind would have stopped them colliding while leaving them plainly
10931               	; 	' visible on the shelf, and a fixture that is still there has to still be
10932               	; 	' there. That was a reason to UNDRAW them, not a reason to keep them --
10933               	; 	' and it left the one hazard that cannot leave on its own as the only one
10934               	; 	' the mercy did not cover. haz_off now takes the characters with it.
10935               	; 	'
10936               	; 	' NOTHING RESTORES IT HERE. load_band repopulates the band from the
10937               	; 	' template, and it runs only on a seam crossing or a round start, so
10938               	; 	' "until the screen is re-entered" costs no state and no timer: leave and
10939               	; 	' come back and the hazards are simply placed again.
10940               	; 	'

11113               	; 	' flight keeps the floor he left until he arrives at the next one. So
11114               	; 	' while he was most of a storey up or down the stairs he still counted as
11115               	; 	' standing on the floor he started from, and a Kop who ran over the head
11116               	; 	' of the flight arrested him through the floor. Reported from play:
11117               	; 	' "I run over top of him, even though we do not touch".

11120               	; 	' separation: a test that is right about one axis and silent about the

11238               	; 	' placed him at his old floor and then hid him again. That is not free.
11239               	; 	' CVBasic's SPRITE writes a RAM mirror which the vblank ISR copies to
11240               	; 	' VRAM, so a vblank landing BETWEEN the draw and the hide latches the
11241               	; 	' visible state for a frame -- and draw_actors is long (Kelly, Harry,
11242               	; 	' eight obstacles) while a pass on the lift screen spans two or three
11243               	; 	' frames, so it happened constantly. He flickered at the floor he had
11244               	; 	' just left, which reads as a drawing bug rather than as a journey.
11245               	; 	'
11246               	; 	' Deciding BEFORE drawing costs one test and cannot race the ISR at all:
11247               	; 	' the mirror never holds a position to be caught with.

11458               	; 		' FOUR RUN FRAMES FROM TWO BITS of the animation counter, and no
11459               	; 		' divide -- `/` compiles to a real TMS9900 DIV (CLAUDE.md 3A) and
11460               	; 		' this is per-frame code. Two adjacent bits give 0,4,8,12.
11461               	; 		'
11462               	; 		' KELLY USES BITS 2 AND 3 AND HARRY USES 3 AND 4, because a stride
11463               	; 		' has to cover about a stride's worth of ground or the figure
11464               	; 		' skates. Kelly runs 4 px a frame, so four frames a pose is 16 px;
11465               	; 		' Harry runs 1.75, so eight frames a pose is 14. Matching the two
11466               	; 		' rates to the two speeds is what keeps both looking like running.

12284               	;
12285               	; 	' ======================================================================
12286               	; 	' THE SCANNER
12287               	; 	' ======================================================================
12288               	; 	' Rows 21-23, 16 chars wide, centred: 48 characters whose PATTERNS are
12289               	; 	' poked directly, so a moving dot costs two writes and no name-table
12290               	; 	' traffic. With the flip (DESIGN.md 2a) this is how you know where Harry
12291               	; 	' is at all -- he can be one pixel off-screen and completely invisible.
12292               	; 	'
12293               	; 	' Rows 21-23 all sit in the THIRD screen third, so every scanner pattern
12294               	; 	' is at base 4096 and no third-selection arithmetic is needed.
12295               	; 	'
12296               	; 	' BOTH DOTS ARE WHITE and Kelly's BLINKS. The manual wants Kelly black
12297               	; 	' and Harry white, but this is the TMS9918's two-colours-per-8x1-cell
12298               	; 	' mode: a black dot and a white dot on the same pixel row of the same
12299               	; 	' character cannot both exist. Blinking distinguishes them with one
12300               	; 	' colour, which is what RallyX does with its player dot.
12301               	; 	' THE STEPS MOVE, AND EVERY ESCALATOR ON SCREEN MOVES WITH THEM. A flight
12302               	; 	' is twelve characters -- six per direction, sliced out of a rendered

12304               	; 	' the lot: 96 bytes, no name-table traffic, and the same cost whether one

12333               	; 	' 8 px period, so advancing by the frame delta ALIASES: at fdv 2 the
12334               	; 	' pattern flips between two positions half a period apart and the
12335               	; 	' direction stops being readable, and at fdv 3 the sequence runs 0,3,2,1
12336               	; 	' -- the staircase visibly runs BACKWARDS, carrying its steps down while
12337               	; 	' the rider goes up. That is the wagon-wheel effect, and no amount of
12338               	; 	' phase arithmetic fixes it: a 4-phase cycle can only be stepped by 1.
12339               	; 	'
12340               	; 	' So the ANIMATION is the clock here, and the rider is paced from it --
12341               	; 	' see move_kelly, which advances him by the same fixed 2-and-1 per pass
12342               	; 	' rather than by fdv. Locking the two together is the only way they
12343               	; 	' cannot drift, and it is what "the player moves at the rate the steps
12344               	; 	' carry him" actually means. The cost is that a ride takes 36 passes
12345               	; 	' rather than 36 frames, so it slows down when the loop does -- which is

12643               	;
12644               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------- the scanner's furniture
12645               	; 	' Without this the scanner is two dots in a void: you can see THAT Harry is
12646               	; 	' somewhere, but not what he is near, which is the one thing you actually
12647               	; 	' need when he is off-screen. Floor lines say which level, the slashes say
12648               	; 	' where that floor's escalator is, and the bar says where the elevator is --
12649               	; 	' exactly the three things the manual lists.
12650               	; 	'
12651               	; 	' FURNITURE AND DOTS ARE SEGREGATED BY PIXEL ROW ON PURPOSE, and a level
12652               	; 	' band is now FOUR rows, one per colour, because a pixel row carries
12653               	; 	' exactly one colour here:
12654               	; 	'
12655               	; 	'   +0  GREY    escalator head, and the elevator car
12656               	; 	'   +1  GREY    the air of that floor
12657               	; 	'   +2  GREY
12658               	; 	'   +3  YELLOW  the floor line -- and NOTHING else goes here
12659               	; 	'
12660               	; 	' THE FIRST THREE ROWS ARE THE FLOOR'S AIR AND EVERYTHING LIVES IN THEM:
12661               	; 	' the escalator's three-step diagonal, the lift car, and both actors, all
12662               	; 	' three pixels tall. They are grey in the table, and the Kop and the
12663               	; 	' crook recolour their own CHARACTER as they move (scan_mark) -- which is
12664               	; 	' what lets both of them fill the band instead of getting a pixel row
12665               	; 	' each. Eight pixels of this canvas is half a screen of the store, so

13954               	;
13955               	; 	' THE BONUS IS COUNTED OUT, NOT AWARDED. Dropping the whole sum into the
13956               	; 	' score in one frame tells the player a number; ticking the clock down a
13957               	; 	' unit at a time, with the score climbing and a beat under each step,
13958               	; 	' tells them what the number was FOR. It is the pay-off for every second
13959               	; 	' they saved, and every arcade game of this era spends a moment on it.
13960               	; 	'
13961               	; 	' It also costs nothing to get right: the loop already has to run down
13962               	; 	' `tsec`, so the animation IS the calculation, and the repeated-addition
13963               	; 	' note below stops applying -- each step adds one band's worth.
13964               	; 	'
13965               	; 	' x100 for Krooks 1-9, x200 for 10-15, x300 from 16. Two independent
13966               	; 	' sources agree on those bands; the manual's own wording suggests
13967               	; 	' 1-8 / 9-16 / 17+ and DESIGN.md 0 records the disagreement.
13968               	; 	'
13969               	; 	' IN UNITS OF TEN, WHICH IS WHAT THE SCORE IS COUNTED IN, so the bands are
13970               	; 	' 10 / 20 / 30 and not 100 / 200 / 300.
13971               	; 	'
13972               	; 	' They were 100 / 200 / 300 and paid TEN TIMES the right bonus -- 1,000 a
13973               	; 	' time unit where the original pays 100. `add_score` takes `#addv` in units
13974               	; 	' of ten (the prize beside it is `#addv = 5` for fifty points, and the bonus
13975               	; 	' Kop threshold is `#nextk = 1000` for ten thousand), so writing the band in
13976               	; 	' POINTS here shifted every tally one decimal place. Reported from play as
13977               	; 	' "it seems like you awarded 1000 per time unit left" -- exactly right.
13978               	; 	'
13979               	; 	' Nothing failed: 1,000 a unit is a plausible-looking number, the digits
13980               	; 	' all line up, and the only symptom is a score that runs away. The tell is
13981               	; 	' a constant written in a different unit from the routine it is passed to,
13982               	; 	' which is the same class of fault as the px-per-pass speeds in 3A.
13983               	; 	'
13984               	; 	' (This is also why the old comment here said "#bval MUST BE 16-BIT: 300
13985               	; 	' does not fit in a byte". At 10 / 20 / 30 it would, but it stays 16-bit
13986               	; 	' because `#addv` is, and a byte here would buy two bytes of ROM in
13987               	; 	' exchange for a truncation trap the next time somebody edits a band.)
13988               	; bonus_count:

14104               	;
14105               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.
14106               	; 	'
14107               	; 	' Two were tried. The bench's own ending for this variant rose a fourth,
14108               	; 	' to 2,542 Hz, and a square wave there is a shriek -- the same fault the
14109               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
14110               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
14111               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
14112               	; 	'
14113               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
14114               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
14115               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
14116               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
14117               	; 	' counting stops.
14118               	;
14119               	; 	' `calc_bonus` USED TO LIVE HERE and computed the whole sum by repeated
14120               	; 	' addition, to dodge two hazards at once: `tsec * bmul` is an 8-bit
14121               	; 	' product (a 50-unit capture in the x300 band pays 15,000, six times past
14122               	; 	' a byte), and multiplying properly lands on the MPY/r0 hazard where a
14123               	; 	' 16-bit variable read straight after being multiplied returns the
14124               	; 	' product's high word. Counting the bonus out a unit at a time (above)
14125               	; 	' removes the multiply entirely rather than working around it -- the loop
14126               	; 	' the player watches IS the arithmetic.
14127               	; 	'
14128               	; 	' It also fixed the last-tick case for free: `bn_loop` tests `tsec = 0`
14129               	; 	' on entry, where the old `FOR bi = 1 TO tsec` would have run its body
14130               	; 	' once and paid a full multiplier for no time at all (CLAUDE.md 3A).

14430               	;
14431               	; 	' A SOUND STILL PLAYING WHEN THE ROUND ENDS IS ALLOWED TO FINISH.
14432               	; 	'
14433               	; 	' This used to open with a bare `GOSUB snd_off`, which cut it dead. That
14434               	; 	' was not an accident: the decay counters are ticked by the MAIN LOOP, and
14435               	; 	' this pause REPLACES the main loop, so a tone left latched with nothing
14436               	; 	' ticking it hangs for the full ninety frames -- the sticky-audio failure
14437               	; 	' this game has already shipped twice. The answer is to DRAIN the counters
14438               	; 	' rather than to stop silencing.
14439               	; 	'
14440               	; 	' CLEAR THE PENDING LATCHES FIRST. sf* flags are sounds that have not
14441               	; 	' happened yet; left set, the drain below would START one and the pause
14442               	; 	' would end with a fresh note ringing into the next round.
14443               	; 	'
14444               	; 	' THEN TICK sfx_tick WHOLE, not some decay-only part of it. The five
14445               	; 	' counters do not all live in one place: sot, sht and spt are a block at
14446               	; 	' the tail, but spz (the prize arpeggio) and swt (the jump warble) tick up
14447               	; 	' among the code that starts sounds. Draining only the tail would finish a
14448               	; 	' footstep and still cut the arpeggio, which is the one effect with a
14449               	; 	' phrase worth saving. Calling the whole routine also leaves the write
14450               	; 	' order on CHANNEL 2 alone, which spz and spt share.
14451               	; 	'
14452               	; 	' EVERY THIRD FRAME, because the main loop runs about 2.5 frames per pass
14453               	; 	' and this loop waits one frame per turn. Ticking every frame would play
14454               	; 	' everything at two and a half times its tuned speed. Three frames a tick
14455               	; 	' is ~17% slow and gives 30 ticks against the longest effect's 20 passes.
14456               	; 	'
14457               	; 	' THE LOOP COUNTS TICKS, NOT FRAMES, which is what makes the pacing free.
14458               	; 	' Counting 91 frames and firing on every third needs a second counter, an
14459               	; 	' increment and a test -- 48 bytes, on a fixed area with 66 left. Counting
14460               	; 	' 31 TICKS of three WAITs each is the same 93 frames and the same three
14461               	; 	' frames per tick, with none of that. The duration changes by two frames.
14462               	; 	'
14463               	; 	' snd_off still runs at the END, as the backstop for anything the drain
14464               	; 	' did not finish.
14465               	; pause_beat:
14466               cvb_PAUSE_BEAT

14828               	;
14829               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
14830               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
14831               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
14832               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
14833               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
14834               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
14835               	;
14836               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
14837               	; 	'
14838               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
14839               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
14840               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
14841               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
14842               	; 	'
14843               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
14844               	; 	'
14845               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
14846               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
14847               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
14848               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
14849               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
14850               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
14851               	; 	'
14852               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
14853               	; 	'
14854               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
14855               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
14856               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
14857               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
14858               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
14859               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
14860               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
14861               	; 	'
14862               	; 	' MEASURED OFF THE COLECOVISION: 14 px, about 7.4 a second.
14863               	; 	'
14864               	; 	' It was 15 px and 6.9 a second, picked between an 8.0 that read as
14865               	; 	' slightly hurried and a 6.1 that read as trudging -- a judgement between
14866               	; 	' two other judgements, with nothing underneath it. The ColecoVision
14867               	; 	' recording settles it: footfalls land every 0.130 s across a twelve-second
14868               	; 	' continuous run, which is 7.7 a second, and that is the one finding in the
14869               	; 	' whole sound analysis the method resolves EXACTLY -- a rhythm rather than a
14870               	; 	' pitch, counted off the RMS track rather than inferred from a spectrum.
14871               	; 	' (colecosounds variant 1A; assets/sfx/sfxref-coleco.md has the working.)
14872               	; 	'
14873               	; 	' 104 px/s over 14 px is 7.43 a second. 13 px would give 8.00, and 7.7 sits
14874               	; 	' almost exactly between them -- so this is the nearer of the two, and it is
14875               	; 	' also the one that does not walk back into the 8.0 that was rejected by ear.
14876               	; 	'
14877               	; 	' WHY THE GAME KEEPS A DISTANCE AND THE BENCH KEEPS A CADENCE. The bench
14878               	; 	' plays a fixed eight frames between steps because it has no walking to tie
14879               	; 	' them to; the game accumulates PIXELS TRAVELLED, so the feet keep time with
14880               	; 	' the legs when he is slowed or stopped. Matching "7.4 a second" therefore
14881               	; 	' means matching it AT HIS WALKING SPEED, and assumes the ColecoVision's
14882               	; 	' crook walks at ours -- which the recording cannot confirm.
14883               	; 	'
14884               	; 	' The dial is this one constant and the subtraction below, which must stay
14885               	; 	' threshold + 1 or the carry is wrong.
14886               	; 	'
14887               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
14888               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
14889               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
14890               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
14891               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
14892               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
14893               	; 	'
14894               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
14895               	; 	'
14896               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
14897               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the
14898               	; 	' whole round. At 13 they were level with the events they are supposed to
14899               	; 	' sit beneath, so the effects that carry information had nothing to stand
14900               	; 	' out from. The tone version was 7 for the same reason -- noise does read
14901               	; 	' quieter than a tone at the same number, which is why this is 9 and not
14902               	; 	' back to 7.
14903               	; 	IF sfw > 13 THEN

15101               	;
15102               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
15103               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
15104               	; 	'
15105               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
15106               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
15107               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
15108               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
15109               	; 	'
15110               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
15111               	; 	'
15112               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
15113               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
15114               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
15115               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
15116               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
15117               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
15118               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
15119               	; 	'
15120               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
15121               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
15122               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
15123               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
15124               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
15125               	; 	'
15126               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
15127               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
15128               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
15129               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
15130               	; 	#if TI994A
15131               	; 	BANK 2
15132      01EC     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$

15610               	; 	' ITS MESSAGE BOXES DID NOT COME WITH IT. They are the same format and
15611               	; 	' were in the same generated file, which is what made this worth doing
15612               	; 	' carefully: they are walked when a ROUND ENDS, mid-game, so on bank 2
15613               	; 	' they would have returned bytes from the wrong page at the moment a life
15614               	; 	' is lost -- and with no error at build or run time. gentitle.py now
15615               	; 	' writes them to title.bas below, which stays in bank 1.
15616               	; 	INCLUDE "titledl.bas"
15617               	; 	' ==================================================
15618               	; 	' THE TITLE SCREEN, AS A DISPLAY LIST
15619               	; 	' Generated by assets/gentitle.py -- do not edit here.
15620               	; 	'
15621               	; 	' row, col, length, then `length` bytes; 255 ends.
15622               	; 	' Walked by title_draw only.
15623               	; 	'
15624               	; 	' LIVES IN BANK 2, with the fonts, because it is read ONCE
15625               	; 	' -- at boot and on a return to the title. title_draw
15626               	; 	' selects bank 2 around its walk and restores bank 1.
15627               	; 	' The message boxes in title.bas are the same format and
15628               	; 	' CANNOT come with it: they are read when a round ends.
15629               	; 	' ==================================================
15630               	;
15631               	; title_tbl:

15824               	; 	INCLUDE "art.bas"
15825               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
15826               	; 	'
15827               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
15828               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
15829               	; 	' being small sprites.
15830               	; 	'
15831               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
15832               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
15833               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
15834               	; 	'
15835               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
15836               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
15837               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
15838               	;
15839               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/the four merged run bodies/duck hat/face/body, then the same LEFT (+36). The run bodies carry tunic AND legs, so a frame is one sprite. Patterns 0..68
15840               cvb_SPR_KELLY

17080               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
17081               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
17082               	; 	'
17083               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
17084               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
17085               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
17086               	; 	'
17087               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
17088               	; 	' blit is
17089               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
17090               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
17091               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
17092               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
17093               	; 	'
17094               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
17095               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
17096               	; 	'
17097               	; 	' template ids:
17098               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
17099               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
17100               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
17101               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
17102               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
17103               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
17104               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
17105               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
17106               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
17107               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
17108               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
17109               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
17110               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
17111               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
17112               	; 	'   14 T_END_E
17113               	;
17114               	; stor_tpl:	' 15 templates x 160 bytes
17115               cvb_STOR_TPL
